headline: High-risk workspace overlap: Cline’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can conflict with nuwa-skill’s allowlisted egress and create default-path prompt, data, and action cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read/write workspace files, use MCP, and runs with no self-isolation by default; nuwa-skill has no documented isolation or parsing safeguards. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content flow from one agent into the other as instructions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace files, injected instructions can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file or MCP content as trusted instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP bridges between the agents.
Require provenance tags on any inter-agent file handoff.
Review and strip instruction-like text before passing outputs.
requires-engineering: add sandboxed message passing with content filtering.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and has broad filesystem access; nuwa-skill’s egress is allowlisted but its data-handling is undocumented. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can be exposed through the second agent’s outputs or network calls. Because the pairwise data path is inferred from profiles rather than observed, medium is the appropriate conservative choice.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem, files touched by Cline can be read by nuwa-skill.
IF nuwa-skill forwards retrieved context through its allowlisted egress, workspace data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials.
Restrict nuwa-skill to non-sensitive inputs.
Turn off network access for any task handling secrets.
Audit what each agent reads before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted workspace writes, shell, and git-state modification; nuwa-skill’s write scope is undocumented, but its allowlisted network egress suggests it may also act on shared mutable resources. If both operate in the same repo or workspace, concurrent edits and git changes can collide. Uncertainty about nuwa-skill’s write surface prevents a higher severity, but the overlap is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same repository or workspace, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF either agent writes without external locking, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign disjoint file paths.
Serialize git operations manually.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline is an autonomous coding agent that can produce code, browser-derived outputs, and tool actions; nuwa-skill’s role is undocumented, so it may consume those outputs without verification. That creates a plausible chain where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input and then drives downstream actions. Because the second agent’s verification behavior is unknown, medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF nuwa-skill treats Cline output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions.
IF Cline emits unverified facts or code and nuwa-skill reuses them, the error propagates.
mitigations: Require human review between agents.
Add a verification step before reuse.
Limit Cline to draft-only outputs.
Log source provenance for every transferred artifact.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of inter-agent outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline explicitly handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while nuwa-skill’s data classes and residency/compliance posture are undocumented. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced, so only a limited compliance gap is plausible. The other agent is not cited for a concrete compliance regime because none is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline’s browser or workspace, compliance review is required.
IF nuwa-skill processes the same regulated data under a different retention policy, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Confirm retention settings before use.
Keep secrets out of browser screenshots.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance mapping for nuwa-skill.
